transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE); Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE); Jae Kim (Redwood Product); Rita Osei (Intellab CTO); Tom Barlow (Intellab ML Eng); Priya Nair (Intellab Platform)

Summary:
Light-weight Optimize walkthrough focused on choosing and validating quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8) for Intellab's inference workload. Showed console flows, sandbox benchmarks, and a proposed pilot plan. Customer concerned about tail-case fidelity loss on sensitive prompts and about VPC/on-prem constraints.

Topics covered:
- Quick intro and goals (latency target, quality SLO)
- Console demo: Profile selection, fallback rules, and rollout UI
- Bench results: synthetic vs prompts from Intellab
- Tradeoffs: INT8 throughput vs FP8 fidelity; mixed-precision strategies
- Pilot proposal and next steps

Action items (recorded in notes): see metadata fields.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh this is Lena from Redwood, i'll hand off to Marco for the demo in a sec but first quick round-robin, rita can you confirm goals?
[00:12] Rita Osei: yeah thanks lena, main thing is we need to cut per-token cost and reduce 95th perc latency from ~420ms to under 220ms for short responses, but cannot see quality regressions on legal/medical style prompts — those are high sensitivity.
[00:28] Tom Barlow: and to add, our infra is a hybrid setup, we want to start hosted sandbox but may move to private VPC; also our prompts have long tail 1-2% of queries that trigger long contexts.
[00:43] Lena Park: ok perfect, so today goal: show how Optimize helps pick profiles (int8 / fp8), run a small bench with your prompts, and propose a pilot that keeps a safety rollback.
[00:55] Marco Ruiz: alright jumping into the console, if you look at the Optimize tab — couple notes, sorry console sometimes labeled "Opti-mize" in older exports, but here's the playbook. we have pre-built profiles: int8_high_performance, fp8_high_fidelity and a hybrid auto-swing profile.
[01:12] [01:12] (screen share starts, slight audio hiss)
[01:22] Marco Ruiz: here's the latency histogram from a sandbox run — you can toggle sample sizes; this one is synthetic tokens. int8 gets us 1.8x throughput on V100-style nodes but we do see a small BLEU-ish style drop for some answer types.
[01:40] Priya Nair: when you say BLEU-ish do you mean nlg metrics or human eval?
[01:45] Marco Ruiz: sorry bad phrasing — we mean automated evals (ROUGE / exact match) plus our fidelity regression tests that you can upload. human evals still recommended for edge-case prompts.
[01:59] Rita Osei: can you show the rollback/fallback? this is the main safety control for us.
[02:05] Marco Ruiz: yes — on the rollout tab you can set policy: percent rollout, latency cap, and a fallback to fp8 or full-precision. so if int8 output fails the quality checks or latency goes over SLO, requests are routed to the fp8 profile or another model variant.
[02:23] [02:23] (typing noises)
[02:30] Tom Barlow: how do you detect the quality fails in real-time? we can't wait hours for human evals.
[02:36] Jae Kim: good q — we support prompt-level assertions and lightweight classifiers that run locally to flag syntactic/semantic anomalies, plus rolling A/B with a small human review queue. also guard rails: exact match checks on specific fields in structured outputs.
[02:52] Tom Barlow: ok that helps. what about quant sensitivity on our named-entity heavy prompts — we saw hallucinations previously with a competitor int8 deploy.
[03:00] Marco Ruiz: so the sensitivity is real; we recommend a three-step approach: 1) profile-level pre-checks (run on a representative sample), 2) stress tests at tail latencies and long context, 3) progressive rollout with canary and fallback. for named-entities we usually bias to fp8 for those routes or keep an exception set.
[03:21] [03:21] (customer mmm)
[03:28] Lena Park: quick commercial note — int8 will give you the biggest unit-cost drop but fp8 sits in the middle: near fp16 fidelity for many models but with throughput quite close to int8 in our newer kernels. Marco will show a heatmap.
[03:42] Marco Ruiz: right, here's a heatmap from our Optimize lab: x-axis is prompt complexity, y is metric delta (fidelity). the rightmost bucket — long legal prompts — shows fp8 losing <1% metric vs fp16, while int8 loses 3–6% in some templates. those numbers vary by model family.
[04:05] Rita Osei: are those numbers from your public benchmarks or from a similar customer?
[04:10] Marco Ruiz: a mix; we seeded with public model runs and then adjusted for closed-customer sandboxes. important note: our kernel selection sometimes chooses mixed-int8-fp8 paths for attention layers to keep critical ops in higher precision — that's the hybrid we mentioned.
[04:27] [04:27] (brief pause, someone on mute)
[04:40] Tom Barlow: on the sandbox, can we run a sweep that measures 99th perc latency too? our SLA concern is tail latency spikes under burst.
[04:48] Marco Ruiz: yes we'll include p50/p95/p99 in the bench. we'll also show cost per 1k tokens at each profile with and without KV caching enabled. note: KV cache is sometimes transcribed as K V cash in older transcripts, sorry for the confusion.
[05:05] Priya Nair: about VPC — if we need a private deployment later, how portable are the profiles and tooling? we can't re-run full quantization again.
[05:14] Jae Kim: portability is a focus — profiles are exported as JSON (profile id + kernel hints + fallback rules). for private deployments the same profile file can be applied; only the binary operator kernels differ per hardware but our compilation step maps them. small tuning pass may be needed when you change GPU family.
[05:33] Rita Osei: ok what would you recommend for our initial pilot then?
[05:38] Lena Park: recommended pilot: start hosted sandbox with three profiles — baseline fp16, fp8_fidelity, int8_perf — run your 500 sample prompts with 3 loads: steady, burst, long-context. we'll collect fidelity deltas, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and cost metrics. after that, pick candidate routes for hybrid rollout.
[05:57] [05:57] (Marco shares a link)
[06:02] Marco Ruiz: link to sandboxes and the quant spreadsheet: https://console.redwood.ai/sandbox/intellab-jan (note: sample link for meeting). spreadsheet has rows: prompt_id, prompt_text redacted, baseline_score, fp8_score, int8_score, latency_p95, notes.
[06:20] Tom Barlow: can you preserve prompt privacy? some of our prompts are PHI-adjacent.
[06:25] Marco Ruiz: yes we have redaction options; for the benchmark you can upload hashed prompts or synthetic variants. sandbox logs can be kept in your VPC if you prefer private deployment.
[06:35] Rita Osei: what about regulatory/compliance — we need audit logs and key management.
[06:40] Lena Park: we support KMS integrations and detailed audit trails, plus SOC 2 attestation. we'll share the security pack.
[06:49] [06:49] (short cross-talk)
[07:02] Marco Ruiz: demoing the console's profile editor now — you can change bitwidth hints, set attention fallback to fp32 for certain layers, or configure a regexp to flag outputs and route to a fallback profile. here's an example rule: if response contains a date range pattern and confidence <0.8 route to fp8.
[07:28] Tom Barlow: interesting. is the confidence computed by the model or a separate estimator?
[07:33] Marco Ruiz: we use a lightweight estimator that runs in the serving path, it's a few extra ms but the estimator can be run async for non-blocking checks.
[07:45] Priya Nair: run-of show me the UI for progressive rollout percent?
[07:51] Marco Ruiz: sure — slider, plus thresholds. you can also pin customer id hashes to a profile for exceptions.
[08:00] [08:00] (screen scrolls to benchmark tab)
[08:12] Marco Ruiz: now to show a real prompt set — Rita shared a sanitized sample earlier, we loaded 200 prompts. here's delta: average fp8 fidelity -0.6% vs baseline, int8 -2.9%; latency p95: baseline 420ms, fp8 260ms, int8 180ms. those are sandbox numbers on our T4-like hardware.
[08:40] Rita Osei: that int8 drop worries me for legal extracts. do you have examples where int8 fails gracefully?
[08:47] Marco Ruiz: typical failure modes: small factual errors, truncation on long contexts, and slight paraphrase differences. fallback rules mitigate this by sending flagged cases to fp8. plus you can configure sampling thresholds to favor precision for named-entity routes.
[09:05] [09:05] (customer audible sigh)
[09:12] Tom Barlow: what's the effort to run your bench on our private hardware (NVIDIA H100 on-prem)? our infra team is wary of re-quantizing.
[09:20] Jae Kim: for H100 we provide a prebuilt runner that maps kernels; typically a light re-calibration (not full quant) is enough — 2–4 hours for the sample set. full model re-quant can be done but isn't required if you're using our hybrid strategy.
[09:37] Rita Osei: do you support blind A/B evaluation or only canary? we want to run blind human eval on a subset.
[09:44] Lena Park: yes blind A/B is supported via the Console — you can route 50/50 and collect human labels in a small review queue integrated with the dashboard.
[09:56] Marco Ruiz: small nit — human review adds latency to the review path but it's async so production serving unaffected.
[10:03] [10:03] (camera briefly on then off)
[10:15] Tom Barlow: ok cost math — can you give a rough example of savings per 1M tokens?
[10:21] Marco Ruiz: rough numbers: baseline fp16 cost $X per 1k tokens (placeholder in demo), fp8 is ~30% lower, int8 is ~55% lower on unit compute. exact depends on throughput and cache hit rates. we'll put exact numbers in the spreadsheet for your runs.
[10:39] Priya Nair: about cache hit rates — how often do we see prefix caching help? our app has many similar prompts.
[10:45] Marco Ruiz: for templated prompts you can get 40–70% token reuse, big wins. but with long-tail unique prompts the benefit shrinks. Optimize suggests routes to enable KV caching per route.
[10:57] [10:57] (brief pause)
[11:10] Rita Osei: any red flags you see from the sample we uploaded?
[11:15] Marco Ruiz: early read shows 6 routes that likely need fp8 by default due to entity density. we'll flag those in the report.
[11:24] Tom Barlow: will you show the raw diffs so our legal team can validate no hallucinated clauses?
[11:30] Lena Park: yes we'll export diff artifacts and you can run your own scripts against them — we can also provide a webhook to push flagged diffs to your audit queue.
[11:39] [11:39] (link pasted)
[11:45] Marco Ruiz: i pasted the sandbox & spreadsheet link in chat again: https://console.redwood.ai/sandbox/intellab-jan
[11:53] Rita Osei: last compliance q: do you keep logs longer than 30 days by default? we need 12 months for audit.
[11:59] Lena Park: hosted default is 30 days but for enterprise/private we support longer retention as an add-on; we'll include retention options in the pricing pack.
[12:12] Tom Barlow: any known incompatibilities with our current auth (SAML + Okta)?
[12:18] Jae Kim: SAML/Okta is supported for Console SSO and we map roles to RBAC in the control plane. for private deployment we'll support your existing IdP.
[12:28] [12:28] (some chatter about calendar invites)
[12:40] Lena Park: ok wrapping up, quick recap: we'll give you sandbox access, run the 3-load benchmark with p50/p95/p99 and fidelity deltas, and reconvene next week. Marco will lead the bench and Tom will provide prompts. action owners in notes.
[12:58] Rita Osei: sounds good thanks all — prioritize the named-entity routes in the report.
[13:05] Marco Ruiz: noted.
[13:10] Lena Park: i'll follow up with security pack + pricing options. thanks everyone.
[13:18] [13:18] (meeting ends)
